subject: stonefish
title: Stonefish Hide a Switchblade Under Each Eye

scenes.text: Stonefish carry a switchblade hidden in their face.
Scientists only described it in 2018: a spine under each eye, called the lachrymal saber.
At rest, it lies flat against the head, pointing back and down.
When the fish is threatened, cheek muscles pull, and the blade swings out ninety degrees.
A tiny locking joint holds it upright, like a knife clicking open.
In one Australian species, the blade even glows green. The rock that stings also has a knife.

description:
Stonefishes have a hidden spine below each eye, the lachrymal saber, described by University of Kansas researchers in Copeia in 2018.
The bone normally lies against the head; when threatened, the fish rotates it about 90 degrees and locks it in place. In one species, Centropogon australis, the saber glows green under blue light.
What other fish would you not want to step on?
first_comment: Every stonefish the researcher examined had the saber. Which is scarier, the venom or the blade?
